source_excerpts.text:
**The proposed universal equality is false.** A two-sender, one-output beam-splitter channel already gives a strict operational rate outside the **entire** Gaussian time-sharing region you defined.

Take the rational channel
\[
X_1=\frac35 I_2,\qquad X_2=\frac45 I_2,\qquad Y=0,
\]
and the fixed budgets
\[
p:=2^{-256},\qquad E_1=p,\qquad E_2=1.
\]

Then
\[
\boxed{
(80p,0)\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{MAC}}(p,1)
\setminus\mathcal R_G(p,1).
}
\]

The exclusion has an explicit margin: every point in the full Gaussian hull satisfies \(R_1<73p\), while the constructed finite code family achieves
\[
R_1=116(\ln2)p>80p.
\]

There is also an explicit point with **both rates positive**:
\[
\boxed{
\left(\frac{396}{5}p,\frac1{1000}\right)
\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{MAC}}(p,1)
\setminus\mathcal R_G(p,1).
}
\]

The Gaussian upper bound below covers arbitrary seed squeezing, modulation and energy time sharing. It even permits unlimited Gaussian helper energy. The achievable construction uses fixed Fock states, pulse-position modulation and individual photon measurements, followed by classical decoding.

The complete proof and exact arithmetic certificate are in [Gaussian_MAC_Strict_Separation_20261108.zip](https://chatgpt.com/library?file_id=libfile_88753389a6c88191823f49a0f728e49a&account_id=personal).

## 1. The channel and the mechanism

Write
\[
b=\sqrt\eta\,a_1+\sqrt{1-\eta}\,a_2,
\qquad \eta=\frac9{25}.
\]
The other beam-splitter output is discarded. This is exactly the stated rational Gaussian channel. Its complete-positivity condition holds at equality:
\[
X(\Omega\oplus\Omega)X^T
=\left(\frac9{25}+\frac{16}{25}\right)\Omega
=\Omega.
\]

The beam-splitter MAC is the standard bosonic multiple-access model studied by Yen and Shapiro. Their coherent-state region and sum-rate results do not establish the full independent-encoder region considered here. [arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/quant-ph/0506171?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
